A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original matrix-sensing and matrix-completion experiments comparing G&C, gradient descent, and prior sampling across network configurations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain original experiments and add threshold-sensitivity results, deeper-network results, and prior-sampling comparisons.

M1.justification: The matrix-factorization architecture, losses, gradient-descent updates, and G&C sampling-and-acceptance procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C's ground-truth-centered distribution is introduced as a theoretical case, rather than a new proposed learning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic low-rank matrix sensing and matrix completion, including rank-one and rank-two targets. Changes concern model configurations and experimental settings within this retained coverage; the higher-rank discussion in the new Appendix D is theoretical.

E2.justification: V2 adds the prior-only sampling comparator to depth comparisons in Figures 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 11, where v1 compared only G&C and gradient descent. Momentum-GD remains the comparator in Figures 3–4 despite its legend changing from 'Momentum' to 'GD'.

E3.justification: Width sweeps extend from 160 to 640. New Figure 12 tests training thresholds 0.025 and 0.03 alongside the existing 0.02 setting. Figure 13 extends G&C to depth 20 using 5 billion draws, with GD omitted beyond depth 10. Existing metrics, target dimensions, and principal training settings remain.

E4.justification: New Figure 12 tests sensitivity to the G&C acceptance threshold, while Figure 13 checks persistence of the depth trend beyond the previous range. Figure 11 removes the unnormalized Leaky ReLU experiment because sampling was computationally prohibitive. The other activation, momentum, rank, prior-distribution, and normalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report medians and interquartile ranges over eight trials differing in random seed. The larger draw budget for Figure 13 changes Monte Carlo sampling effort, not the reported number of independent trials or the uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for prior-only depth comparisons, larger widths, depths through 20, and alternative acceptance thresholds, while removing Figure 11's Leaky ReLU results. These largely corroborate the existing width-deterioration and depth-improvement findings. The new unnormalized-prior curves also show improving prior-only generalization with tanh.

T1.justification: New Appendix D develops a higher-rank depth argument using Lyapunov exponents and Laplace's principle, explicitly leaving full formalization for future work. Appendix C changes Theorem 9 from a zero-ground-truth case to a distribution shifted around the ground truth. Definition 4 also corrects the derivative-growth condition to use absolute values. The two principal theorems and their underlying proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the novelty claim from the first provable inferiority of G&C to the first such canonical case with conventional priors. New footnote 1 acknowledges that contrived counterexamples are straightforward. The central contrast between increasing width and increasing depth remains.

C2.justification: V2 clarifies that the depth guarantee bounds generalization loss by a constant times the training threshold; increasing depth alone need not match GD or produce zero loss. It adds the computational consequence of shrinking that threshold and explains the unnormalized tanh prior's improvement through convergence toward the zero matrix. The higher-rank extension is explicitly qualified as unproved.

D1.justification: Appendix H and Tables 1–5 document settings for the added experiments, including the additional thresholds and Figure 13's 5-billion-draw budget. The code-access information, PyTorch implementation, A6000 hardware, batching procedure, and existing optimization details are retained from v1's Appendix G.

R1.justification: V2 adds literature connecting depth to expressiveness and implicit bias, discusses tensor-factorization extensions, and cites adaptive optimizers and their generalization behavior. It also refines novelty around canonical counterexamples. The central positioning against Chiang et al. and Peleg and Hein remains; many other reference edits are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The proof sketches in Sections 4.2–4.3 are substantially expanded to explain their existing mathematical ingredients. Appendix C reorganizes the proof into four stages covering density convergence, characteristic functions, bounded-set approximation, and the final argument. The conclusion is expanded with practical implications and tensor-factorization directions, alongside language and cross-reference editing.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are broadly revised: width plots receive expanded axes, depth plots add prior curves and legends, and Figure 11 changes from three activation panels to two. Figures 12–13 are added, and the settings tables gain entries and move. These are display and layout changes beyond numerical updates alone.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the existing evidence through prior-only depth comparisons and threshold/depth checks, while making the novelty claim and depth guarantee more precise. Expanded proof explanations also improve accessibility. The gains are limited: the principal results remain unchanged, the higher-rank argument is explicitly unformalized, and the unnormalized Leaky ReLU experiment is removed. Overall, the revision improves support and interpretation without resolving the main theoretical restrictions.
